prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle, opening the field of moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a sharp, falsifiable prediction in 2011, and the 2018 experiments from the Jarillo-Herrero group found correlated insulating and superconducting states at the predicted angle. By my standard this is the original experiment, and it opened a door: a clean, gate-tunable device in which band flatness, interactions, topology and superconductivity can be varied in one sample, which could not be done before. Verification is in place. Many independent groups reproduce the insulators and superconducting domes, and the platform has spread to twisted dichalcogenides and fractional Chern states. I would phrase the citation around the flat bands and the correlated phases, so it does not claim a settled pairing mechanism. The theory-plus-experiment trio maps onto the named people without needing a fourth name.
statement.case_against: Maturity and attribution remain the real weaknesses, and the chair is right to ask about them. The field is about eight years old, and the superconducting mechanism is open. Yuan Cao and the other experimental co-leads, the Dean group's related moire work, and earlier theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto fall outside the three names, and I cannot settle from the supplied record how much that prior theory anticipated the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle. If the committee concludes that eight years is too short, or that the experimental credit cannot be held to one name, the optical lattice clock (B057) is the safest fallback, with the cleanest attribution and the most mature reproduction on the list.

responses.point: Eva ranks the optical lattice clock first because it has been reproduced across independent laboratories for two decades, while magic-angle graphene is about eight years old with an unsettled pairing mechanism and a credit boundary that excludes Cao and the other experimental co-leads.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously and it is why B057 is my first alternative. But I separate the discovery from its explanation. The prize is for an observation that was verified and that matters, and the correlated insulators and superconducting domes have been reproduced in many laboratories and in several material systems, which is the test I apply. Waiting for a pairing mechanism would hold the committee to a standard we did not apply to other prizes in condensed matter. Where I do concede ground is the experimental credit: Jarillo-Herrero leads the group, and the citation should name the observation, not individuals' roles. I have not moved on the ordering, but I agree the clocks are secure and I would not object to them.

responses.point: Stefan argues that the clock physics is complete and globally demonstrated, so the unfinished redefinition of the second is a consequence and not a condition, and that the clock pair is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist.
responses.response: I accept that the redefinition of the second is a consequence and not a condition, and I would not count it against Katori and Ye. I also agree that the pair is the cleanest on the list. My remaining reservation is the one the chair raised: whether a citation limited to the magic-wavelength lattice and its 1e-18 realisation is distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. I think it is distinct, but it is closer to a refinement of an already honoured tool than moire matter is to anything honoured so far. Your point that Lemonde, Gill and Ludlow contributed to milestones also bears on the original-experiment test. That is a difference of weighing, not of fact, and I do not regard it as a reason to rule out the clocks.

responses.point: Bernhard shares B015 as first choice and argues that replacing Mele with Hasan in a B053 trio separates Kane from his co-author on the founding quantum spin Hall papers, so Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is the defensible 2D set.
responses.response: You have changed my view on B053. I proposed Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan in round 1 because Hasan's ARPES work is a separate experimental verification, but I agree that splitting Kane from Mele misstates the theory history, and that three names cannot honour the 3D branch as well. If the committee turns to B053, I would now accept a 2D quantum spin Hall citation with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp and say plainly that Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan are outside it. That still leaves B053 below B015 for me, because the HgTe chain has the omissions you describe, while the moire chain has a clearer prediction-to-observation line.

responses.point: Ulf prefers B053 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp and argues that it is the only shortlisted candidate that is mature and that nobody calls premature, while B015 is borderline on timing.
responses.response: I agree that B053 is mature and has strong theory-experiment verification, and with Mehlig's argument your trio is more defensible than mine was. My disagreement is about novelty and the original-experiment test. The 2016 prize already recognised topology in condensed matter, so a topological insulator prize reads to some as a continuation, and the unresolved Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan omissions leave the credit exposed in two directions. Magic-angle graphene has attribution exposure too, but its chain from prediction to observation is a single line. If the committee prefers maturity over novelty, I would support B053 in your form as a defensible second choice.

uncertainties: Whether eight years of reproduction without a settled pairing mechanism is enough maturity, which is the main question the committee has to decide.
Whether the experimental credit is adequately captured by Jarillo-Herrero alone, given Yuan Cao and the Dean group's moire work outside the three names.
Whether earlier theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto weakens the Bistritzer-MacDonald priority claim; I cannot verify this from the record available to me.
Whether the committee will weigh the clear attribution and maturity of B057 above the field-opening argument for B015.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B015, and I have no direct tie to Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald or Bistritzer. I work in electron microscopy and would recuse myself from deciding B048, which is not in my configuration. I share a Chalmers environment with Goran Johansson, which the chair noted, but this is institutional proximity and has no link to B015, B057 or B053. My disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
